avg_teacher_rating.name: avg_teacher_rating
avg_teacher_rating.definition: Arithmetic mean of TeacherRating across unique instructors.
avg_teacher_rating.caveat: Evaluation reflects student perception of instructor directly.

avg_course_rating.name: avg_course_rating
avg_course_rating.definition: Arithmetic mean of CourseRating across unique course catalog titles.
avg_course_rating.caveat: Independent of enrollment volumes; reflects catalog baseline quality.

rating_consistency_index.name: rating_consistency_index
rating_consistency_index.definition: Enrollment-weighted mean of per-instructor course quality consistency (1 - CV_weighted).
rating_consistency_index.caveat: Instructor-to-instructor differences do not exceed chance (permutation p = 0.406), so the index describes portfolio mix rather than instructor reliability.

experience_impact_teacher_rating.name: experience_impact_teacher_rating
experience_impact_teacher_rating.definition: Annual rating increase per year of instructor teaching experience (OLS on TeacherRating).
experience_impact_teacher_rating.caveat: Experience strongly predicts teacher rating (r = +0.598, p < 0.0001).

experience_impact_course_rating.name: experience_impact_course_rating
experience_impact_course_rating.definition: Annual course quality rating change per year of teaching experience (OLS on weighted CourseRating).
experience_impact_course_rating.caveat: Teaching experience does not translate into higher course quality ratings (slope = -0.0035, p = 0.666).

experience_impact.name: experience_impact
experience_impact.definition: Annual rating increase per year of instructor teaching experience.
experience_impact.caveat: Experience strongly predicts teacher rating but has negligible translation into course quality.

enrollment_influence.name: enrollment_influence
enrollment_influence.definition: Ratio of high-tier enrollment share to instructor population representation.
enrollment_influence.caveat: Platform enrollments are sensitive to superstar concentration: most of the High tier's enrollments come from 4 instructors (see leave-top-k sensitivity).

F1.question: What are the distributional characteristics and normality of instructor ratings?
F1.method: Summary stats, Shapiro-Wilk normality test, Bootstrap CIs
F1.notes: Instructor ratings average 3.125 (median 3.275, IQR 1.340, five-number summary: min 1.050, Q1 2.487, median 3.275, Q3 3.827, max 4.970, skewness -0.485). Shapiro-Wilk normality test: W=0.962, p=0.0583.

F2.question: Does instructor experience predict higher instructor rating?
F2.method: Pearson r (Fisher-z CI), Spearman rho, OLS linear slope
F2.notes: Experience is positively correlated with TeacherRating (r = 0.598, p = 4.5176e-07, slope = 0.120 rating points/year). Excluding >=15 yrs yields r = 0.553 (p = 8.2893e-06).

F3.question: Does instructor experience transfer to higher course ratings?
F3.method: Teacher-level Pearson r vs Pair-level Cluster-Robust OLS
F3.notes: At teacher level (n=60), experience vs weighted course rating is r = -0.057 (p = 0.6659, negligible effect). At pair level (n=887), naive p-value is 0.6960, and cluster-robust standard errors yield slope = -0.0024 (p = 0.3566).

F4.question: Is there an experience threshold or nonlinear plateau in instructor ratings?
F4.method: Two-group Mann-Whitney U, Piecewise OLS breakpoint search, LOWESS smoother
F4.notes: 0–5 yrs (n=28, mean=2.399) vs 6+ yrs (n=32, mean=3.760): mean difference = +1.361 rating points [95% CI: 1.03, 1.70], Mann-Whitney U = 839.0, p = 7.1863e-09 (large effect). The 0–5 vs 6+ group difference is supported, but a specific breakpoint is not supported (candidate b*=8 yrs, permutation p = 0.124).

F4a.question: Do instructors with 6+ years of experience receive significantly higher ratings than instructors with 0–5 years?
F4a.method: Two-group Mann-Whitney U test with bootstrap CI of mean difference
F4a.notes: 0–5 yrs (n=28, mean=2.399) vs 6+ yrs (n=32, mean=3.760): mean difference = +1.361 rating points [95% CI: 1.03, 1.70], Mann-Whitney U = 839.0, p = 7.1863e-09 (large effect).

F4b.question: Is there an optimal piecewise-linear breakpoint threshold in instructor ratings?
F4b.method: Piecewise-linear OLS breakpoint search with permutation benchmark
F4b.notes: Piecewise breakpoint search identified candidate b*=8 yrs (delta-R2 = 0.0636, slope pre = +0.212, slope post = +0.048), but permutation p = 0.124 >= 0.05 indicates no statistically significant breakpoint.

F5.question: Are instructor ratings correlated with the quality ratings of the courses they teach?
F5.method: Multi-level correlation (Teacher n=60, Course n=60, Secondary Pair n=887 with cluster-robust SE)
F5.notes: Teacher-level correlation is r = 0.000 (p = 0.9971). Course-level correlation is r = -0.013 (p = 0.9212). Secondary pair-level cluster-robust OLS gives slope = -0.0391 (p = 0.0929). Instructor performance and course quality are statistically decoupled (rating_decoupling = True).

F6.question: Do course quality ratings differ significantly across course categories?
F6.method: Kruskal-Wallis H test with epsilon-squared effect and Holm post-hoc
F6.notes: Kruskal-Wallis across course categories: H = 4.388 (df = 11, p = 0.9572, epsilon^2 = 0.000, negligible effect). Category differences in course rating are not statistically significant. 29 cells in Category x Level have n < 3.

F7.question: Do course quality ratings vary by course difficulty level?
F7.method: Kruskal-Wallis across levels and Mann-Whitney U for Advanced vs Intermediate
F7.notes: Kruskal-Wallis across levels: H = 1.913 (df = 2, p = 0.3842, epsilon^2 = 0.000, negligible effect). Advanced vs Intermediate contrast: mean diff = -0.509 [95% CI: -1.18, 0.18] (Mann-Whitney U = 137.0, p = 0.1468).

F8.question: Do instructor ratings or course quality vary by gender and course level?
F8.method: Teacher-level Mann-Whitney U with Holm adjustment & Transaction-level cluster-bootstrapped cells
F8.notes: (a) TeacherRating by Gender: Mann-Whitney U = 551.0, raw p = 0.119, Holm-adj p = 0.119 (not supported). (b) Course quality by Gender: Mann-Whitney U = 254.0, raw p = 0.0045, Holm-adj p = 0.0091 (Male higher; difference may reflect which courses each gender teaches and data cannot establish cause). (c) Transaction-level Gender x Level cells are descriptive.

F8a.question: Do instructor ratings (TeacherRating) differ significantly by gender?
F8a.method: Teacher-level Mann-Whitney U test with Holm-Bonferroni family adjustment
F8a.notes: Females (n=27, mean=3.231, median=3.460) vs Males (n=33, mean=3.038, median=3.100): Mann-Whitney U = 551.0, raw p = 0.1187, Holm-adj p = 0.1187 (rank-biserial = -0.237, small effect).

F8b.question: Do course quality ratings differ between courses taught by female vs male instructors?
F8b.method: Teacher-level Mann-Whitney U test on weighted CourseRating with Holm-Bonferroni adjustment
F8b.notes: Courses taught by Male instructors receive higher enrollment-weighted ratings (Male n=33, mean=3.247, median=3.237 vs Female n=27, mean=3.053, median=3.012). Mean difference (Female - Male) = -0.195 [95% CI: -0.339, -0.052], Mann-Whitney U = 254.0, raw p = 0.0045, Holm-adj p = 0.0091 (rank-biserial = 0.430, moderate effect). Difference may reflect which courses each gender teaches; the data cannot establish a cause.

F8c.question: What is the enrollment-weighted course quality across Gender x CourseLevel cells?
F8c.method: Transaction-level aggregation with teacher-cluster bootstrap CIs
F8c.notes: Gender x Level table (6 cells): enrollment-weighted CourseRating with teacher-cluster bootstrap CIs. Differences describe portfolio allocation; data cannot establish causation.

F9.question: Do High-tier instructors teach higher-rated courses than Mid or Low-tier instructors?
F9.method: Kruskal-Wallis across tiers on teacher_table with Holm post-hoc
F9.notes: Kruskal-Wallis across instructor tiers: H = 0.068, p = 0.9668, epsilon^2 = 0.000. Tier means on weighted course rating: High=3.17, Mid=3.14, Low=3.17. Differences are not significant.

F10.question: Do higher-rated instructors attract significantly more student enrollments?
F10.method: Teacher-level Spearman rho with bootstrap CI and High-tier vs rest contrast
F10.notes: Spearman correlation between TeacherRating and total enrollments is rho = -0.012 (p = 0.9274). High-tier instructors vs rest Mann-Whitney: U = 383.5, p = 0.030 (High tier mean=620.0, Mid tier mean=56.3, Low tier mean=76.4).

F11.question: Is enrollment driven by instructor rating or concentrated in specific domains?
F11.method: Inequality indices (Gini, Top-N, HHI), Leave-k-out sensitivity, Robust domain-controlled OLS
F11.notes: Teacher enrollment Gini = 0.681, Top-5 share = 65.5%, Top-11 share = 73.1%, HHI = 1885.7. Within top 2 domains (n=14): rho = 0.319 (p = 0.266); excluding top 2 (n=46): rho = 0.031 (p = 0.837). Controlling for domain in OLS (HC3), TeacherRating slope on log(enr) is beta = 0.164 (SE = 0.187, p = 0.3823, partial R2 = 0.027). Singletons: ['Marketing', 'Programming']. Course concentration: Gini = 0.042, Top-5 course share = 9.5%.

F12.question: Do instructor ratings vary systematically across expertise domains?
F12.method: Kruskal-Wallis H test across domains (reporting both min_group_size 2 and 3)
F12.notes: Kruskal-Wallis across expertise domains: [min_group_size=3 headline, 9 groups, n=56]: H = 15.196 (df = 8, p = 0.0554, epsilon^2 = 0.153); [min_group_size=2 secondary, 10 groups, n=58]: H = 15.670 (df = 9, p = 0.0741, epsilon^2 = 0.139). Expertise area differences in TeacherRating are not statistically significant.

F13.question: How does course quality vary by expertise domain, and is there an ML quality gap?
F13.method: Domain-specific aggregation, cluster CIs, and ML quality contrast
F13.notes: Machine Learning Quality Contrast: ML category catalog average CourseRating (A, n=5) is 2.658 (held fixed) vs enrollment-weighted CourseRating of courses taught by ML instructors (B, n=5 teachers) of 3.055 (unweighted 2.946). Point estimate (B - A) is +0.397; teacher-cluster bootstrap distribution mean is 0.289 (offset from small-cluster ratio estimation bias, n=5); 95% cluster CI is [-0.066, 0.418] and bootstrap two-sided p = 0.163 >= 0.05 (verdict: not supported). ML instructors' TeacherRating averages 4.234 (reported separately). Mean own-domain teaching share across platform is 74.0%.
